locators.excerpt:
## Numerical and serialization limits

The mechanics source uses Python float operations, sequential trapezoid accumulation and scalar three-/two-item arithmetic means. The reference model uses NumPy float64 schedule arithmetic and exponentials; transformations cast to float32 only after standardization. Independently authored tests compare analytic signals and a separate sum formulation; the private source-differential check additionally executes isolated original arithmetic on invented inputs only. Cross-platform transcendental bit identity is not claimed; exact differential equality is recorded for the qualified local environment.

The earlier world-generation source declares decimal rounding to nine places and canonical sorted-key compact JSON. The inspected pre-final shadow code converts NumPy scalars to Python floats and serializes JSON without that explicit rounding step. These are **distinct source paths**, neither a verified final-split serialization lineage. This phase does not assign either behavior to every historical Gate7 row, regenerate the historical split, recompute its labels or scores, or resolve the generic canonical force/impulse crosswalks.

All basis components are computable at origin **if and only if** the complete relevant history, origin duration, future plan snapshots and forecast query are authenticated as known at that origin. Future event execution is not an input. The source's synthetic generator supplies a predetermined plan; it does not prove prospective availability in an empirical archive. The source basis function itself performs no availability or rights checks.

Original preprocessing constructs raw/history/basis arrays from the same ordered input-row list, with no separate key join. The basis matrix is float64 `(N,5)`; history is float64 `(N,4,4)`, oldest to latest; horizon is int64 H72=0/D7=1. Every external row must preserve participant/origin/query/input identity across these tensors. Train-only basis means and sample standard deviations (`ddof=1`) are frozen in each checkpoint configuration; zero training scales become one. Standardize using those frozen statistics, then cast tensors to float32. No cohort fitting is needed or permitted for original preprocessing. M6 validates/preprocesses all five basis values but consumes only the first two; M7 consumes five; M8 consumes five in its nonlinear and linear basis branches. No fitted values are published here.

locators.excerpt:
The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Holm adjustment covers the locked primary candidate's four zero-improvement tests. Other candidate comparisons are exploratory. Each primary cell must additionally have a paired RMSE-improvement CI lower bound strictly greater than its prespecified margin, RMSE/MAE upper bounds within the harm limits, its bias interval inside the signed bounds, enough participants and an adjusted p-value <=0.05. All four cells must pass. Failure is reported explicitly; an engineering fixture can correctly produce `criteria_not_met`. The test and margin guard have different documented roles. This implementation does not infer power or research success from synthetic outcomes.

The earlier world-generation source declares decimal rounding to nine places and canonical sorted-key compact JSON. The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Holm adjustment covers the locked primary candidate's four zero-improvement tests. Other candidate comparisons are exploratory. Each primary cell must additionally have a paired RMSE-improvement CI lower bound strictly greater than its prespecified margin, RMSE/MAE upper bounds within the harm limits, its bias interval inside the signed bounds, enough participants and an adjusted p-value <=0.05. All four cells must pass. Failure is reported explicitly; an engineering fixture can correctly produce `criteria_not_met`. The test and margin guard have different documented roles. This implementation does not infer power or research success from synthetic outcomes.

Run `python -m cmj_recovery_dynamics.metrics.native_rehearsal --synthetic-rehearsal` outside or inside an installed environment. It creates a new, explicitly invented labeled fixture; admits it through preflight; fits an invented training-only constant; pairs 18 candidate/repeat combinations; computes four-cell analysis; and exercises refusal controls. Predictions are intentionally constructed from invented labels and errors to test arithmetic; they are not evidence of prediction performance. No recovered weights or original records are used.

The JSON receipt includes source/contract identities, plan/input/prediction hashes, counts, exclusions, RNG and quantile conventions, all contrasts, cell-level decisions and an explicit false empirical-execution authorization. It contains no timestamp, so identical inputs/environment produce identical receipts. Tests independently expand sampled participant rows, including unequal cluster sizes and repeated participant draws, and compare numerical metrics/intervals; known Holm examples and sign-flip tie cases are also checked. A bracketing sample beyond takeoff can support interpolation at the event, but its timestamp/value is not included as a separate integration node. For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. The event contract requires `movement_start < t_co < t_to <= assessment_end`; the scored events must lie inside the supplied force-time domain. The authenticated source does **not** implement empirical event detection from force thresholds or velocity zero crossings: it accepts event times from the caller. Thus no detector threshold or instrument-specific filter can be claimed as source-authorized by this specification.

The original numerical rule accepts finite strictly increasing, potentially nonuniform timestamps. At an exact-sample event, use the original sample once. Otherwise linearly interpolate the boundary force from its two bracketing samples. Retain original samples strictly inside the interval and integrate the closed support `[t_co,t_to]` by sequential composite trapezoids. A bracketing sample beyond takeoff can support interpolation at the event, but its timestamp/value is not included as a separate integration node. The terminal contact force is the supplied/interpolated value at takeoff, not a subsequent airborne value. Net force is subtracted at support nodes before integration. The original velocity cross-check starts its identity coordinate at zero velocity at `t_co`; this arbitrary offset is not an empirical absolute velocity estimate.

locators.excerpt:
## Five-value basis: closed source construction

This is a **fixed nominal public-schedule basis**, not a fitted physiological dose or an inferred latent state. Original source consumes only each row's `history_exposures`, `known_plan` and `target_time_hours`. Each duration is divided by **100 minutes**, producing dimensionless dose `d_i`. Events are sorted as `(time_hours, dose)` tuples; the original function skips events after target time `T`. No assessment value or target label enters the computation.

The index exposure is already a time-zero entry in the original query-specific `known_plan`. Do not append `index_exposure` separately. The recovered public observation converter follows this convention. The new constructor validates one pre-origin historical exposure, two/three query-specific plans, distinct event times, exactly one matching time-zero plan, nonnegative finite durations and each plan's `known_at_origin=True`. These admission safeguards are stricter than the original arithmetic function, which trusts the supplied schedule. A boolean assertion alone does not prove availability; source snapshots/version timestamps must authenticate it outside this constructor.

| 4 | `w3_slow_increment_weighted` | `sum Δ_i*w_120(i)` | dimensionless |

Constants: fast 36 h, slow 120 h, beta 1, kappa 10, delta 1. Gamma 1 is declared in the original configuration but is **not separately used** by its rational `_w3` arithmetic; this is not an adjustable gamma implementation. Values at target time receive decay weight one. Zero-duration events contribute zero, and an all-zero schedule returns five zeros. Empirical durations and plans must actually exist; no fabricated exposure events or physiological mappings are permitted.

All basis components are computable at origin **if and only if** the complete relevant history, origin duration, future plan snapshots and forecast query are authenticated as known at that origin. Future event execution is not an input. The source's synthetic generator supplies a predetermined plan; it does not prove prospective availability in an empirical archive. The source basis function itself performs no availability or rights checks.

## Metrics and comparisons

The four separate cells are force in N/kg and impulse in m/s at H72 and D7. Signed error is prediction minus observed additive innovation. The query-weighted estimates are RMSE, MAE and signed bias, accompanied by cell participant/query counts. No averaging across incompatible units occurs. Each repeat is reported separately; the family estimate is the arithmetic mean of the two per-repeat metrics, never an ensemble of their predictions. Repeat disagreement is descriptive, not a predictive interval.

Zero innovation is the prespecified primary comparator. An optional separate constant artifact can be fitted only from supplied training-group observations. The version-2 artifact binds four ordered native cell means, source authority, the exact designated training participants, the complete training observations including labels, and the training-only arithmetic-mean protocol. Its content hash detects local inconsistency; it is not independent authentication. Validation/test labels are refused by that fitting entry point; the analysis requires a separately trusted `expected_constant_baseline_sha256`, checks that expected identity in addition to local content consistency, and requires the exact designated training groups. Substituting values and recomputing the artifact hash cannot replace that expected pin. The trusted caller must obtain the pin from the approved fitting step or an authenticated fit receipt, never from the incoming artifact. Missing pins and old version-1 artifacts are refused. The engineering rehearsal uses a separately frozen pin for its invented training fixture. All fitting and qualification here use invented values only. No historical OLS comparator is silently introduced.

## Paired uncertainty and hypothesis test

A locked NumPy PCG64 generator first draws a `(resamples, participants)` array of participant indices with replacement, then, only above 16 participant groups, a same-shaped array of -1/+1 signs for the separate hypothesis test. Participant identities are sorted. The bootstrap retains every query, origin, horizon, target, candidate, repeat and baseline of each drawn participant. Repeated draws multiply the participant's contribution; clusters with more queries retain their larger query weight. Every comparison uses the identical draw array. At least 10,000 resamples are required.

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Holm adjustment covers the locked primary candidate's four zero-improvement tests. Other candidate comparisons are exploratory. Each primary cell must additionally have a paired RMSE-improvement CI lower bound strictly greater than its prespecified margin, RMSE/MAE upper bounds within the harm limits, its bias interval inside the signed bounds, enough participants and an adjusted p-value <=0.05. All four cells must pass. Failure is reported explicitly; an engineering fixture can correctly produce `criteria_not_met`. The test and margin guard have different documented roles. This implementation does not infer power or research success from synthetic outcomes.

Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

The original numerical rule accepts finite strictly increasing, potentially nonuniform timestamps. At an exact-sample event, use the original sample once. Otherwise linearly interpolate the boundary force from its two bracketing samples. Retain original samples strictly inside the interval and integrate the closed support `[t_co,t_to]` by sequential composite trapezoids. A bracketing sample beyond takeoff can support interpolation at the event, but its timestamp/value is not included as a separate integration node. The terminal contact force is the supplied/interpolated value at takeoff, not a subsequent airborne value. Net force is subtracted at support nodes before integration. The original velocity cross-check starts its identity coordinate at zero velocity at `t_co`; this arbitrary offset is not an empirical absolute velocity estimate.

The new `native_force_metrics_v1` independently implements only this deterministic arithmetic. A caller still authenticates event detection, full event ordering/domain, signal calibration, protocol metadata and trial validity. Reject nonfinite input, non-increasing timestamps, invalid support, nonpositive mass/gravity and nonfinite numerical output. Additional finite-real and overflow safeguards do not claim historical acceptance behavior.

## Trials, assessments, baseline and labels

All basis components are computable at origin **if and only if** the complete relevant history, origin duration, future plan snapshots and forecast query are authenticated as known at that origin. Future event execution is not an input. The source's synthetic generator supplies a predetermined plan; it does not prove prospective availability in an empirical archive. The source basis function itself performs no availability or rights checks.

Original preprocessing constructs raw/history/basis arrays from the same ordered input-row list, with no separate key join. The basis matrix is float64 `(N,5)`; history is float64 `(N,4,4)`, oldest to latest; horizon is int64 H72=0/D7=1. Every external row must preserve participant/origin/query/input identity across these tensors. Train-only basis means and sample standard deviations (`ddof=1`) are frozen in each checkpoint configuration; zero training scales become one. Standardize using those frozen statistics, then cast tensors to float32. No cohort fitting is needed or permitted for original preprocessing. M6 validates/preprocesses all five basis values but consumes only the first two; M7 consumes five; M8 consumes five in its nonlinear and linear basis branches. No fitted values are published here.

Validation/test labels are refused by that fitting entry point; the analysis requires a separately trusted `expected_constant_baseline_sha256`, checks that expected identity in addition to local content consistency, and requires the exact designated training groups. Substituting values and recomputing the artifact hash cannot replace that expected pin. The trusted caller must obtain the pin from the approved fitting step or an authenticated fit receipt, never from the incoming artifact. Missing pins and old version-1 artifacts are refused. The original criterion is the arithmetic mean of exactly **three valid trials** with distinct trial IDs, one assessment identity and one assessment timestamp. Every trial passes signal, event, mechanical and protocol validation; invalid trials are not silently imputed, replaced, dropped or selected by performance. The source uses scalar sums divided by three, not a best-of-three or median criterion. Explicit depth is reference COM position minus bottom COM position in m, nonnegative, with source positions retained; it is not inferred from a velocity-drift proxy.

The baseline is the arithmetic mean of the two latest distinct valid qualifying assessment summaries in the inclusive **24–240-hour pre-origin interval**. The original selector sorts descending by `(assessment_time, assessment_id)`, then keeps the first occurrence of each identity. It skips invalid or internally mismatched assessment records. Tied assessment times therefore have an implementation tie-break, but do not establish that empirical duplicates are independent assessments. The preflight layer must reject ambiguous/contradictory identity records rather than reinterpret them as new assessments.

H72 is nominal 72 h, assessment window **66–78 h**; D7 is nominal 168 h, window **156–180 h**, relative to the registered origin. Both native targets refer to the same assessment/time per query. The four cells remain separate; N/kg and m/s are never pooled. Target selection and all baseline identities must be locked and authenticated; a nominal visit name does not prove its timestamp.

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

locators.excerpt:
The original criterion is the arithmetic mean of exactly **three valid trials** with distinct trial IDs, one assessment identity and one assessment timestamp. Every trial passes signal, event, mechanical and protocol validation; invalid trials are not silently imputed, replaced, dropped or selected by performance. The source uses scalar sums divided by three, not a best-of-three or median criterion. Explicit depth is reference COM position minus bottom COM position in m, nonnegative, with source positions retained; it is not inferred from a velocity-drift proxy.

The baseline is the arithmetic mean of the two latest distinct valid qualifying assessment summaries in the inclusive **24–240-hour pre-origin interval**. The original selector sorts descending by `(assessment_time, assessment_id)`, then keeps the first occurrence of each identity. It skips invalid or internally mismatched assessment records. Tied assessment times therefore have an implementation tie-break, but do not establish that empirical duplicates are independent assessments. The preflight layer must reject ambiguous/contradictory identity records rather than reinterpret them as new assessments.

H72 is nominal 72 h, assessment window **66–78 h**; D7 is nominal 168 h, window **156–180 h**, relative to the registered origin. Both native targets refer to the same assessment/time per query. The four cells remain separate; N/kg and m/s are never pooled. Target selection and all baseline identities must be locked and authenticated; a nominal visit name does not prove its timestamp.

## Numerical and serialization limits

The mechanics source uses Python float operations, sequential trapezoid accumulation and scalar three-/two-item arithmetic means. The reference model uses NumPy float64 schedule arithmetic and exponentials; transformations cast to float32 only after standardization. Independently authored tests compare analytic signals and a separate sum formulation; the private source-differential check additionally executes isolated original arithmetic on invented inputs only. Cross-platform transcendental bit identity is not claimed; exact differential equality is recorded for the qualified local environment.

The earlier world-generation source declares decimal rounding to nine places and canonical sorted-key compact JSON. The inspected pre-final shadow code converts NumPy scalars to Python floats and serializes JSON without that explicit rounding step. These are **distinct source paths**, neither a verified final-split serialization lineage. This phase does not assign either behavior to every historical Gate7 row, regenerate the historical split, recompute its labels or scores, or resolve the generic canonical force/impulse crosswalks.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Holm adjustment covers the locked primary candidate's four zero-improvement tests. Other candidate comparisons are exploratory. Each primary cell must additionally have a paired RMSE-improvement CI lower bound strictly greater than its prespecified margin, RMSE/MAE upper bounds within the harm limits, its bias interval inside the signed bounds, enough participants and an adjusted p-value <=0.05. All four cells must pass. Failure is reported explicitly; an engineering fixture can correctly produce `criteria_not_met`. The test and margin guard have different documented roles. This implementation does not infer power or research success from synthetic outcomes.

## Reproduction and verification

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. The original model has 10,796 parameters: a 39→64→64 raw backbone, a one-layer 4→32 GRU with mean/latest pooling, a 2×8 horizon embedding, a 5→16 basis projection, a 152→2 residual head and a bias-free 5→2 basis head. Both basis paths consume all five standardized basis values.

Authenticated original configurations, checkpoints, source and validation identities were checked privately. Original fitted preprocessing and all four forward-input tensors were compared for the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. For each repeat, recovered inference matched original CPU source exactly and was deterministic. Input tensor and private prediction identities are retained in the private receipt; no trained weights or restricted observations are distributed.

CPU-to-saved-CUDA comparisons use the original rule `abs(replayed-saved) <= 1e-5 + 1e-4*abs(saved)`. Both failed: r0 maximum absolute difference 0.00022125244140625 with 98 of 1,024 elements outside tolerance; r1 maximum 0.00030422210693359375 with 145 outside tolerance. Historical CUDA compatibility is not established. The fixed CPU TF32 approximation had zero tolerance failures for both repeats; it is an explanatory diagnostic, not an authentic CUDA replay. Historical runtime attribution remains unresolved.

CPU source parity does not establish predictive accuracy, generalization, robustness, clinical applicability, production readiness or checkpoint redistribution rights. The existing rights and release decisions remain unchanged.

The original model has 10,796 parameters: a 39→64→64 raw backbone, a one-layer 4→32 GRU with mean/latest pooling, a 2×8 horizon embedding, a 5→16 basis projection, a 152→2 residual head and a bias-free 5→2 basis head. Both basis paths consume all five standardized basis values.

Authenticated original configurations, checkpoints, source and validation identities were checked privately. Original fitted preprocessing and all four forward-input tensors were compared for the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. For each repeat, recovered inference matched original CPU source exactly and was deterministic. Input tensor and private prediction identities are retained in the private receipt; no trained weights or restricted observations are distributed.

`metrics.native_analysis` is a synthetic-only analysis implementation. It preserves the separately versioned native measurement/identity contract; it does not use generic canonical targets, calibrate a historical score, authorize empirical execution, or load checkpoints. A caller declaration cannot establish that records really are synthetic. Both the evaluator and training-constant constructor reject a non-synthetic dataset kind, even if supplied permission decisions claim approval. A future empirical path requires separate review and authorization.

The plan must explicitly lock its primary candidate, four target/horizon rules with native units, RMSE improvement margins, maximum RMSE/MAE and absolute signed-bias bounds, minimum participant counts, analysis unit, confidence-interval method, multiplicity family, test method/assumption, random seed, resamples and exclusions. There are no default scientifically meaningful margins. Rehearsal thresholds are hypothetical engineering inputs, with no clinical or human-validity interpretation. Every candidate requires repeats r0 and r1 on exactly the same query/target rows. Preflight stages for structure, measurement authority, independence, use, result generation and result disclosure must all pass and the preflight receipt must be pinned. The analysis admission receipt binds the exact dataset, source authority, participant splits, native observations and inspected preflight payload fingerprint; a receipt for another file is rejected. These are separately reviewed declarations, not permissions inferred from a valid file.

## Metrics and comparisons

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

The original model has 10,796 parameters: a 39→64→64 raw backbone, a one-layer 4→32 GRU with mean/latest pooling, a 2×8 horizon embedding, a 5→16 basis projection, a 152→2 residual head and a bias-free 5→2 basis head. Both basis paths consume all five standardized basis values.

Authenticated original configurations, checkpoints, source and validation identities were checked privately. Original fitted preprocessing and all four forward-input tensors were compared for the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. For each repeat, recovered inference matched original CPU source exactly and was deterministic. Input tensor and private prediction identities are retained in the private receipt; no trained weights or restricted observations are distributed.

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Run `python -m cmj_recovery_dynamics.metrics.native_rehearsal --synthetic-rehearsal` outside or inside an installed environment. It creates a new, explicitly invented labeled fixture; admits it through preflight; fits an invented training-only constant; pairs 18 candidate/repeat combinations; computes four-cell analysis; and exercises refusal controls. Predictions are intentionally constructed from invented labels and errors to test arithmetic; they are not evidence of prediction performance. No recovered weights or original records are used.

The JSON receipt includes source/contract identities, plan/input/prediction hashes, counts, exclusions, RNG and quantile conventions, all contrasts, cell-level decisions and an explicit false empirical-execution authorization. It contains no timestamp, so identical inputs/environment produce identical receipts. Tests independently expand sampled participant rows, including unequal cluster sizes and repeated participant draws, and compare numerical metrics/intervals; known Holm examples and sign-flip tie cases are also checked. Receipt hashes establish byte consistency, not real-world scientific provenance.

Validation/test labels are refused by that fitting entry point; the analysis requires a separately trusted `expected_constant_baseline_sha256`, checks that expected identity in addition to local content consistency, and requires the exact designated training groups. Substituting values and recomputing the artifact hash cannot replace that expected pin. The trusted caller must obtain the pin from the approved fitting step or an authenticated fit receipt, never from the incoming artifact. Missing pins and old version-1 artifacts are refused. The four separate cells are force in N/kg and impulse in m/s at H72 and D7. Signed error is prediction minus observed additive innovation. The query-weighted estimates are RMSE, MAE and signed bias, accompanied by cell participant/query counts. No averaging across incompatible units occurs. Each repeat is reported separately; the family estimate is the arithmetic mean of the two per-repeat metrics, never an ensemble of their predictions. Repeat disagreement is descriptive, not a predictive interval.

Zero innovation is the prespecified primary comparator. An optional separate constant artifact can be fitted only from supplied training-group observations. The version-2 artifact binds four ordered native cell means, source authority, the exact designated training participants, the complete training observations including labels, and the training-only arithmetic-mean protocol. Its content hash detects local inconsistency; it is not independent authentication. Validation/test labels are refused by that fitting entry point; the analysis requires a separately trusted `expected_constant_baseline_sha256`, checks that expected identity in addition to local content consistency, and requires the exact designated training groups. Substituting values and recomputing the artifact hash cannot replace that expected pin. The trusted caller must obtain the pin from the approved fitting step or an authenticated fit receipt, never from the incoming artifact. Missing pins and old version-1 artifacts are refused. The engineering rehearsal uses a separately frozen pin for its invented training fixture. All fitting and qualification here use invented values only. No historical OLS comparator is silently introduced.

## Paired uncertainty and hypothesis test

`metrics.native_analysis` is a synthetic-only analysis implementation. It preserves the separately versioned native measurement/identity contract; it does not use generic canonical targets, calibrate a historical score, authorize empirical execution, or load checkpoints. A caller declaration cannot establish that records really are synthetic. Both the evaluator and training-constant constructor reject a non-synthetic dataset kind, even if supplied permission decisions claim approval. A future empirical path requires separate review and authorization.

The plan must explicitly lock its primary candidate, four target/horizon rules with native units, RMSE improvement margins, maximum RMSE/MAE and absolute signed-bias bounds, minimum participant counts, analysis unit, confidence-interval method, multiplicity family, test method/assumption, random seed, resamples and exclusions. There are no default scientifically meaningful margins. Rehearsal thresholds are hypothetical engineering inputs, with no clinical or human-validity interpretation. Every candidate requires repeats r0 and r1 on exactly the same query/target rows. Preflight stages for structure, measurement authority, independence, use, result generation and result disclosure must all pass and the preflight receipt must be pinned. The analysis admission receipt binds the exact dataset, source authority, participant splits, native observations and inspected preflight payload fingerprint; a receipt for another file is rejected. These are separately reviewed declarations, not permissions inferred from a valid file.

All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Holm adjustment covers the locked primary candidate's four zero-improvement tests. Other candidate comparisons are exploratory. Each primary cell must additionally have a paired RMSE-improvement CI lower bound strictly greater than its prespecified margin, RMSE/MAE upper bounds within the harm limits, its bias interval inside the signed bounds, enough participants and an adjusted p-value <=0.05. All four cells must pass. Failure is reported explicitly; an engineering fixture can correctly produce `criteria_not_met`. The test and margin guard have different documented roles. This implementation does not infer power or research success from synthetic outcomes.

The terminal contact force is the supplied/interpolated value at takeoff, not a subsequent airborne value. Net force is subtracted at support nodes before integration. The original velocity cross-check starts its identity coordinate at zero velocity at `t_co`; this arbitrary offset is not an empirical absolute velocity estimate.

The new `native_force_metrics_v1` independently implements only this deterministic arithmetic. A caller still authenticates event detection, full event ordering/domain, signal calibration, protocol metadata and trial validity. Run `python -m cmj_recovery_dynamics.metrics.native_rehearsal --synthetic-rehearsal` outside or inside an installed environment. It creates a new, explicitly invented labeled fixture; admits it through preflight; fits an invented training-only constant; pairs 18 candidate/repeat combinations; computes four-cell analysis; and exercises refusal controls. Tests independently expand sampled participant rows, including unequal cluster sizes and repeated participant draws, and compare numerical metrics/intervals; known Holm examples and sign-flip tie cases are also checked. Receipt hashes establish byte consistency, not real-world scientific provenance.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. `metrics.native_analysis` is a synthetic-only analysis implementation. It preserves the separately versioned native measurement/identity contract; it does not use generic canonical targets, calibrate a historical score, authorize empirical execution, or load checkpoints. A caller declaration cannot establish that records really are synthetic. Both the evaluator and training-constant constructor reject a non-synthetic dataset kind, even if supplied permission decisions claim approval. A future empirical path requires separate review and authorization.

The plan must explicitly lock its primary candidate, four target/horizon rules with native units, RMSE improvement margins, maximum RMSE/MAE and absolute signed-bias bounds, minimum participant counts, analysis unit, confidence-interval method, multiplicity family, test method/assumption, random seed, resamples and exclusions. There are no default scientifically meaningful margins. Rehearsal thresholds are hypothetical engineering inputs, with no clinical or human-validity interpretation. Every candidate requires repeats r0 and r1 on exactly the same query/target rows. Preflight stages for structure, measurement authority, independence, use, result generation and result disclosure must all pass and the preflight receipt must be pinned. The analysis admission receipt binds the exact dataset, source authority, participant splits, native observations and inspected preflight payload fingerprint; a receipt for another file is rejected. These are separately reviewed declarations, not permissions inferred from a valid file.

## Metrics and comparisons

A locked NumPy PCG64 generator first draws a `(resamples, participants)` array of participant indices with replacement, then, only above 16 participant groups, a same-shaped array of -1/+1 signs for the separate hypothesis test. Participant identities are sorted. The bootstrap retains every query, origin, horizon, target, candidate, repeat and baseline of each drawn participant. Repeated draws multiply the participant's contribution; clusters with more queries retain their larger query weight. Every comparison uses the identical draw array. At least 10,000 resamples are required.

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

## Reproduction and verification

Run `python -m cmj_recovery_dynamics.metrics.native_rehearsal --synthetic-rehearsal` outside or inside an installed environment. It creates a new, explicitly invented labeled fixture; admits it through preflight; fits an invented training-only constant; pairs 18 candidate/repeat combinations; computes four-cell analysis; and exercises refusal controls. Predictions are intentionally constructed from invented labels and errors to test arithmetic; they are not evidence of prediction performance. No recovered weights or original records are used.

The JSON receipt includes source/contract identities, plan/input/prediction hashes, counts, exclusions, RNG and quantile conventions, all contrasts, cell-level decisions and an explicit false empirical-execution authorization. It contains no timestamp, so identical inputs/environment produce identical receipts. Tests independently expand sampled participant rows, including unequal cluster sizes and repeated participant draws, and compare numerical metrics/intervals; known Holm examples and sign-flip tie cases are also checked. Receipt hashes establish byte consistency, not real-world scientific provenance.

## Metrics and comparisons

The four separate cells are force in N/kg and impulse in m/s at H72 and D7. Signed error is prediction minus observed additive innovation. The query-weighted estimates are RMSE, MAE and signed bias, accompanied by cell participant/query counts. No averaging across incompatible units occurs. Each repeat is reported separately; the family estimate is the arithmetic mean of the two per-repeat metrics, never an ensemble of their predictions. Repeat disagreement is descriptive, not a predictive interval.

Zero innovation is the prespecified primary comparator. An optional separate constant artifact can be fitted only from supplied training-group observations. The version-2 artifact binds four ordered native cell means, source authority, the exact designated training participants, the complete training observations including labels, and the training-only arithmetic-mean protocol. Its content hash detects local inconsistency; it is not independent authentication. Validation/test labels are refused by that fitting entry point; the analysis requires a separately trusted `expected_constant_baseline_sha256`, checks that expected identity in addition to local content consistency, and requires the exact designated training groups. Substituting values and recomputing the artifact hash cannot replace that expected pin. The trusted caller must obtain the pin from the approved fitting step or an authenticated fit receipt, never from the incoming artifact. Missing pins and old version-1 artifacts are refused. The engineering rehearsal uses a separately frozen pin for its invented training fixture. All fitting and qualification here use invented values only. No historical OLS comparator is silently introduced.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

Methodological finding: the old p=1 shortcut for nonpositive observed statistics was conservative but was not the full right-tail probability. Both modes now count that same prespecified right tail, including at zero and negative observations; the null, statistic and scientific decision thresholds are unchanged. All-zero losses still give p=1. With six nonzero positive group improvements the smallest exact p is 1/64=0.015625, so the four-cell Holm minimum is 4/64=0.0625 and cannot meet alpha 0.05. Exact p values are discrete and independent of the random seed; bootstrap intervals retain their separately locked seed.

Holm adjustment covers the locked primary candidate's four zero-improvement tests. Other candidate comparisons are exploratory. Each primary cell must additionally have a paired RMSE-improvement CI lower bound strictly greater than its prespecified margin, RMSE/MAE upper bounds within the harm limits, its bias interval inside the signed bounds, enough participants and an adjusted p-value <=0.05. ## Paired uncertainty and hypothesis test

A locked NumPy PCG64 generator first draws a `(resamples, participants)` array of participant indices with replacement, then, only above 16 participant groups, a same-shaped array of -1/+1 signs for the separate hypothesis test. Participant identities are sorted. The bootstrap retains every query, origin, horizon, target, candidate, repeat and baseline of each drawn participant. Repeated draws multiply the participant's contribution; clusters with more queries retain their larger query weight. Every comparison uses the identical draw array. At least 10,000 resamples are required.

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

For every repeat and family, 95% two-sided marginal percentile confidence intervals use NumPy's linear quantile convention. Paired contrasts include candidate-minus-baseline RMSE, MAE and bias; RMSE improvement is baseline-minus-candidate. The family metric is recomputed as a mean of per-repeat metrics in every resample. Confidence intervals are not declared simultaneous or predictive.

The prespecified one-sided participant sign-flip test uses participant sums of zero-baseline squared error minus the mean of the two repeat squared errors. Its null is zero paired squared-error improvement, under independent participant clusters and symmetry of the cluster loss difference under the null. It is not a test of a nonzero RMSE margin and is not distribution-free without that assumption. For 16 or fewer participant groups, enumerate all `2^n` sign allocations and report `count(statistic >= observed) / 2^n`, without a plus-one correction. The bound limits the sign matrix to 65,536 × 16 int64 values (8 MiB); the transient arithmetic arrays remain bounded. For larger cohorts retain sampled allocations and the plus-one Monte Carlo correction `(1 + count(randomized statistic >= observed statistic)) / (B + 1)`. Receipts record exact versus Monte Carlo mode, allocation count, seed (unused for exact testing), enumeration bound and limitations. Monte Carlo tails remain seed-dependent approximations with resolution `1/(B+1)` and possible repeated allocations. A bound derived from float64 epsilon, participant count and absolute loss magnitude conservatively includes numerical ties; the observed and randomized statistics use the same reduction convention.

# Original Gate7 M7 recovery findings

M7 is the original trained candidate, distinct from the earlier M7 remediation milestone. Both final repeats use a 39→64→64 raw backbone, a single-layer 4→32 GRU with mean/latest pooling, a 2×8 horizon embedding, a 5→16 basis projection and a 152→2 head, totaling 10,786 parameters. It consumes all five standardized basis values. Each repeat uses its own authenticated original configuration and fitted preprocessing.

Both repeats reproduced the authenticated original CPU source exactly on the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. These are source-parity results, not predictive validation. The saved historical CUDA predictions did not pass the predeclared rule `abs(replayed-saved) <= 1e-5 + 1e-4*abs(saved)`: repeat 0 had 163 failing elements with maximum absolute difference 0.00031757354736328125; repeat 1 had 198 failing elements with maximum absolute difference 0.00030493736267089844, out of 1,024 elements each. Authentic historical GPU replay has not been established.

# RES-546: original Gate7 M8 recovery

This is the trained Gate7 M8 candidate, distinct from the earlier M8 release and reference-study milestones. Its complete final-repeat set is M8-r0 and M8-r1. The original model has 10,796 parameters: a 39→64→64 raw backbone, a one-layer 4→32 GRU with mean/latest pooling, a 2×8 horizon embedding, a 5→16 basis projection, a 152→2 residual head and a bias-free 5→2 basis head. Both basis paths consume all five standardized basis values.

Authenticated original configurations, checkpoints, source and validation identities were checked privately. Original fitted preprocessing and all four forward-input tensors were compared for the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. For each repeat, recovered inference matched original CPU source exactly and was deterministic. Input tensor and private prediction identities are retained in the private receipt; no trained weights or restricted observations are distributed.

Authenticated original configurations, checkpoints, source and validation identities were checked privately. Original fitted preprocessing and all four forward-input tensors were compared for the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. For each repeat, recovered inference matched original CPU source exactly and was deterministic. Input tensor and private prediction identities are retained in the private receipt; no trained weights or restricted observations are distributed.

CPU-to-saved-CUDA comparisons use the original rule `abs(replayed-saved) <= 1e-5 + 1e-4*abs(saved)`. Historical CUDA compatibility is not established. The fixed CPU TF32 approximation had zero tolerance failures for both repeats; it is an explanatory diagnostic, not an authentic CUDA replay. Historical runtime attribution remains unresolved.

CPU source parity does not establish predictive accuracy, generalization, robustness, clinical applicability, production readiness or checkpoint redistribution rights. The existing rights and release decisions remain unchanged.

It consumes all five standardized basis values. Each repeat uses its own authenticated original configuration and fitted preprocessing.

Both repeats reproduced the authenticated original CPU source exactly on the 24-row synthetic fixture and 512-row historical validation split. These are source-parity results, not predictive validation. Authentic historical GPU replay has not been established.

The fixed CPU TF32 approximation passed this numerical rule for both repeats, but it is only an explanatory diagnostic and does not establish historical CUDA compatibility or the original runtime mechanism.
